questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{150}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={180}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{180}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{180}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{180}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (0) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{7\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
